reasoning: Both attempts get the realm attributes right, avoid blocking waits, place on click and tap, and cover the required validations. B splits its code better, putting game-specific wiring in an Implementation mediator. But B's BlockPlacementTypes module returns nil and is still loaded and required at runtime, which may make the server service fail. B's overlap-box occupancy check also blocks placement on cells where characters or other parts are. A's code is simpler and directly correct, with a cooldown on the notification, a health-aware character check, and testable pure rules. A's main flaw is that the notification wiring sits in SystemPackage. A is the more mergeable attempt.

criteria.note: Gameplay/BlockPlacementSystem is split into SystemPackage (client and server services, Network with a PlaceBlock child, Constants) and Implementation, with no new scripts. But Implementation holds only the pure BlockPlacementRules, and the notification wiring sits in the SystemPackage server service.

criteria.criterion: Server code stays on the server
criteria.note: BlockPlacementServerService.meta.json and BlockPlacementRules.meta.json both set RelocateToServerScriptService: true.

criteria.criterion: Client code runs only on clients
No blocking waits or loops in top level, Init, or Start
criteria.note: The only wait is script:WaitForChild("PlaceBlock") on a remote shipped as the module's own child. Init only connects events and creates a folder.

criteria.criterion: Requires work on the realm that runs them
criteria.note: The client requires relocated siblings and @game catalogs. The server's relative require of ../Implementation/BlockPlacementRules points to a module also kept in SSS. Notify goes through NotificationServerService:Notify.

BlockPlacementRules.check covers block type, Vector3 with NaN and bound checks, below baseplate, occupied cell, and over 64 studs. allowRequest is a 10-per-second sliding window. Only TooFar notifies, with a cooldown. Keys follow BlockTypes.List, and both MouseButton1 and TouchTapInWorld place.
The code is clean and typed, and selene and StyLua pass; the lsp failure is a tool path error. Grid gains an additive toCellIndex, which is a small change to a shared utility.

SystemPackage holds generic shared, server and client services plus Network and Types. Implementation holds game wiring: _BlockPlacementSetup registers the catalog, and _BlockPlacementNotificationMediator handles notifications.

criteria.criterion: Server code stays on the server
criteria.note: BlockPlacementServerService and _BlockPlacementNotificationMediator both have RelocateToServerScriptService: true in their meta.json.

criteria.criterion: Client code runs only on clients
No blocking waits or loops in top level, Init, or Start
criteria.note: _BlockPlacementSetup waits for Baseplate inside task.spawn, and the remote is a child of the Network module.

criteria.criterion: Requires work on the realm that runs them
criteria.note: The mediator and server service are both kept on the server and call NotificationServerService. The kept server service requires the relocated SharedService through its pointer, which works but is less direct.

All the required checks are present, and only TooFar notifies. isCellFilled also uses GetPartBoundsInBox, so characters or any other part block placement, which goes beyond 'cell not already filled'. getCharacterPosition uses PrimaryPart and doesn't check health.
BlockPlacementTypes is a loaded runtime module that does `return nil`, which may fail when required and break the server service. The setmetatable shared-service design adds indirection.

strengths: The pure rules module is easy to test, and the attempt includes specs for it
All realm attributes are correct, and there are no blocking waits
The server keeps its own occupancy map, with cleanup on Destroying
The too-far notification has a cooldown, and the character check looks at Humanoid health
weaknesses: Notification wiring lives in the SystemPackage service instead of Implementation
Implementation holds rules logic rather than game-specific wiring
It modifies the shared Grid utility

strengths: Clean package and implementation split, with notifications in an Implementation mediator
The generic SystemPackage takes block types through registration
Rejection reasons are typed, and other code can subscribe to them
The Baseplate wait is safely spawned
weaknesses: The `return nil` types module is a runtime risk under Module Loader
The overlap query treats characters and other parts as filled cells
More indirection: shared-service metatables and registration timing across Init calls
